channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Report: Diplomats from Arab country support haredi parties joining Eisenkot government
item.description:
Diplomats from an Arab country that maintains diplomatic relations with Israel are closely following negotiations to form a government led by Gadi Eisenkot and view the possibility of the haredi parties joining the coalition favorably, Kan 11 News reported.
According to the report, the diplomats said in closed-door discussions that the haredi parties would be "easier partners to work with" than Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich.

item.title: Limor Sonn Har Melech warns: They will simply be wiped out
item.description: MK Limor Sonn Har Melech calls for new elections and warns parties considering forming a government with the support of Arab lawmakers.

item.title: Reports of vehicles set on fire in Palestinian village in Samaria; security forces dispatched
item.description:
Security forces were dispatched to the Palestinian Arab village of Luban ash-Sharqiya in Samaria following reports of arson and footage from the scene showing vehicles engulfed in flames, the IDF Spokesperson's Unit said.
The IDF stated that "forces are currently operating in the area to locate suspects and restore order. Once the fires have been extinguished, police officers and forensic investigators will enter the area under IDF protection to collect findings and evidence."

item.title: Report: Iran still has 1,700 ballistic missiles, produces 50 monthly
item.description: Western intelligence estimates Iran retains at least 1,700 ballistic missiles and can produce 50 more each month despite extensive US and Israeli airstrikes.

item.description: Police findings submitted to prosecutors find no election financing violations. Likud claims 1,281 complaints of election irregularities remain uninvestigated.

item.title: Minister Gila Gamliel: Likud will not join opposition, unity government is only option
item.description: Minister Gila Gamliel backs Netanyahu's call for a broad-based government, saying neither bloc can govern alone and personal considerations must not stand in the way of unity.

item.title: Netanyahu responds to Board of Peace: "Hamas has not surrendered a single weapon"
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says Hamas's refusal to disarm is preventing Gaza's reconstruction, accusing the terrorist organization of exploiting humanitarian aid to rebuild its military capabilities.

item.title: Next Year in Jerusalem!
item.description: In 1929, Rabbi Avraham Yitzhak HaKohen Kook hosted Rebbe Yosef Yitzhak Schneerson in his Jerusalem home during the Chabad Rabbi's visit to the Holy Land. Rabbi Kook exhorted his distinguished guest to bring his followers to the Chosen Land.

item.title: MK Yitshak Goldknopf: 'We don't belong to anyone'
item.description: At Arutz Sheva's Knesset studio, MK Yitshak Goldknopf said UTJ would follow its rabbis' ruling. He said coalition partners failed haredi needs, blamed the Religious Zionist Party for budget cuts and urged recognition of haredi civilian service.

item.title: Rabbi Dov Lior: Wording of blessings must not be changed during prayers on Temple Mount
item.description: Rabbi Dov Lior clarifies that worshippers praying on the Temple Mount should continue using the customary conclusions to the blessings and should not adopt the wording used when the Holy Temple stood.

item.title: Huckabee: Settler violence? 'A mischaracterization'
item.description: US ambassador to Israel clarifies that Trump has not ruled out further military action against Iran and also addressed political developments in Israel following the elections.

item.title: Revealed meeting between Likud and Yashar canceled
item.description: Following Netanyahu's speech at the Knesset swearing-in ceremony, the Yashar party chairman ordered the cancellation of a planned negotiation meeting with Likud representatives.

item.title: Watch: Minister Wasserlauf's son gives a surprising answer
item.description: Minister Yitzhak Wasserlauf attended the Knesset swearing-in ceremony with his wife and children, when one of his sons was asked whether he was proud of his father and his answer brought a smile to everyone's face.

item.title: 'Fabricated intelligence': Demand to Shin Bet chief follows explosive testimony
item.description: In a letter to the Shin Bet chief, 15 settlers allege that Central Command continues to impose severe restrictions on them without trial or an opportunity to defend themselves.

item.title: Minister Eliyahu warns haredi parties
item.description: Eliyahu calls the unity government proposed by the Prime Minister a "national paralysis government" and warns the haredi parties against "repeating the mistake of Oslo."

item.title: Final Decision: Knesset Speaker to be replaced next week
item.description: Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana announced Tuesday evening that, following an unusual request signed by 67 MKs, a vote to elect his replacement will be held next Tuesday.

item.title: Dedicated ATMs channel money to terrorists
item.description: Lt. Col. (res.) attorney Maurice Hirsch's new study details how the PA funds terrorists and their families via dedicated ATMs and money changers. He criticizes Israeli enforcement, urging seizure of funds and sanctions on recipients.

item.title: A puppet on a string: Yair Netanyahu lashes out at Eisenkot
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu's son attacked Yashar! party chairman, claiming that 'Israel may not survive him.' Eisenkot’s party lashed back.

item.title: Matan Kahana to Arutz Sheva: 'I have a unifying role; we seek a broad Zionist government'
item.description: Knesset speaker candidate Matan Kahana told Arutz Sheva, "I see this as a significant role, a role that unites the citizens of the State of Israel". He also discussed Arab parties' support and a possible unity government.

item.title: Netanyahu: There is no difference between the Joint List and Ra'am
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sharply criticized the Joint List and Ra'am on Tuesday evening, claiming that there is no difference between the two parties' objectives.

item.title: Rare moment of unity: MK who lost both legs in war receives standing ovation
item.description: Newly elected MK Elisha Medan rises on prosthetic legs to take oath of office, drawing applause from across the political spectrum. Herzog and Ohana urge Zionist parties to unite and avoid another election.

item.title: "To whom is he pledging allegiance? Hamas?" Ben Gvir interrupts Jabareen
item.description: A confrontation erupted in the Knesset plenum after Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen declared, "I pledge," provoking an angry reaction from Minister Itamar Ben Gvir.

item.title: Jerusalem race breaks through boundaries
item.description: Around 480 Jewish and Arab runners participated Friday morning in the 12th annual 'Running Without Borders' race in Jerusalem, bringing together families from all parts of the city.

item.title: Ben Gvir interrupts Jabareen - "To whom is he pledging allegiance? Hamas?"
item.description:
A confrontation erupted in the Knesset plenum after Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen declared, "I pledge."
In response, Itamar Ben Gvir interrupted him, shouting, "To whom is he pledging allegiance? Is he pledging allegiance to Hamas?"

item.title: Britain to save historic synagogue
item.description: Restoration funding will be used to repair the roof, renovate the prayer hall, and establish a heritage exhibition commemorating the history of the local Jewish community.

item.title: New MK Shira Shapira, Aner's mother, fought back tears, 'I came because of Aner'
item.description: Incoming Yashar MK Shira Shapira arrived at the Knesset with a photo of her late son Aner, who threw back seven grenades on October 7. Tearfully, she said she had visited his grave before the ceremony, declaring, 'I am here on his behalf.'
